VERDICT: EXTEND C0001 | `scan_health()` also misreports timed-out tools as available, not just missing binaries. Evidence: `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")` on timeout; each runner only special-cases `"NOT_FOUND"` and otherwise returns `[]`; `scan_health()` sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally. This means a timed-out pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy run is logged as available-and-clean, which suppresses a real infrastructure failure in the endocrine report.

VERDICT: CONFIRM C0021

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually sandbox test execution against the patched source tree. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it writes only the patched target file into a temp dir as `tmpdir/<basename>.py`, but `test_cmd` is executed unchanged with only `cwd=tmpdir`. In the real caller path from `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`, the command is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", "-x", "-q", "--tb=no", "--no-header", "-q"]`. That path resolves against the repository, not the temp dir, so pytest imports and exercises the real codebase, while the patched file in tmpdir is usually not on the import path and often has the wrong package location entirely. This makes the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” path a false positive: tests can pass even when the patch breaks runtime behavior, because the patch is never under test.
FOLLOW: The downstream effect is on the core SAFE/HARMFUL verdict used by the immune pipeline’s Stage 4. `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` marks findings `verified=True` when endocrine returns `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL`. Because tests are being run against original source, a harmful patch can be mislabeled SAFE/NEUTRAL if static counts do not increase. That in turn activates the NK “bug closed” gate in later rounds, causing duplicate future findings to be auto-closed around an unverified fix. This crosses the endocrine→immune→insect-brain interface and can silently corrupt review state by closing real bugs.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — create a real sandbox project layout before testing: copy the full source tree (or at minimum all `source_paths` preserving relative paths/package structure) into the temp dir, apply the patch to the copied target file at its original relative path, and run `test_cmd` against that sandbox path so imports resolve to the patched code, not the repository originals.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as `SAFE` even when it introduces new issues in one tool, as long as a different tool’s issue count drops by a larger amount. Evidence: it computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; if `total_net > 0` verdict is `HARMFUL`, if `< 0` verdict is `SAFE`. Example from the implemented fields: `net_type_errors = +3`, `net_ruff_errors = -5`, `net_bandit_issues = 0` yields `total_net = -2` and verdict `SAFE`, despite three new type errors. This contradicts the module docstring and verdict semantics (“SAFE: no new issues introduced”).
FOLLOW: This directly affects Stage 4 in `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`, where `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL` marks a finding `verified=True`. A patch that regresses one verifier while improving another can be accepted and then treated as a programmatically verified closure. The downstream consequence is silent wrong state: harmful fixes become “verified,” duplicate reports are suppressed by the NK bug-closed gate, and the human reviewer sees misleading closure status.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta as `HARMFUL` before considering aggregate improvement: if `net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`, return `HARMFUL`; only return `SAFE` when no per-tool delta is positive and at least one is negative or tests passed.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can apply a finding’s fix to the wrong source file due to substring matching. It extracts any `*.py` token from `finding.description + finding.proposed_fix`, then returns the first `source_paths` entry where `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. The `match in sp_path` branch is unsafe: a short filename fragment can match unrelated paths, and with multiple files sharing substrings/basenames the first incidental match wins. Because the function falls back silently to `source_paths[0]`, fix evaluation can target the wrong file without raising.
FOLLOW: Wrong-file targeting breaks the root promise of fix evaluation. Pre-fix counts are measured on one file, the patch is applied to another or to an unrelated fallback file, post-fix counts are then compared on that wrong file, and the verdict is attributed to the original finding ID. This propagates into `evaluate_fixes()` batch results and then into immune Stage 4 verification, where unrelated findings may be marked verified or unevaluable for the wrong reason. It crosses the endocrine→immune interface and can silently verify the wrong bug.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — resolve target files only by exact canonical match against known source paths or unique basename match; if resolution is ambiguous or absent, return `None` and mark the evaluation `UNEVALUABLE` instead of using substring matching or defaulting to the first source file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the module advertises fix evaluation using static analysis tools including mypy/crosshair in the header, but `evaluate_fix()` only measures pyright, ruff, and bandit before/after. `MYPY_BIN`, `CROSSHAIR_BIN`, and `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT` are declared, and the top-level docstring lists mypy and crosshair as tool binaries, but fix verdicts ignore both. This leaves implemented health-scan coverage and fix-evaluation coverage inconsistent.
FOLLOW: Downstream, a patch that introduces a mypy-detectable regression but no pyright/ruff/bandit regression can be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL and then `verified=True` by the immune pipeline. Because Stage 4 relies on endocrine verdicts to close bugs, this mismatch creates a silent wrong-result path rather than mere incomplete tooling. It also misleads the insect brain/human reviewer about what “programmatically verified” means.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — include mypy in the pre/post fix counts used by `evaluate_fix()` and verdict computation; if crosshair is not intended for PoC fix evaluation, remove it from the advertised fix-evaluation tool list rather than implying it participates.
VERIFIED: TRUE
